nodes.title: Run the counter with OnPush
nodes.why: Everything the template shows comes from a signal, so Angular can skip this component until a signal it reads changes or one of its buttons fires.
nodes.alternative: Keep the default strategy, which checks the component on every change detection pass anywhere in the app.
nodes.tradeoff: OnPush is free here and keeps working if the count later changes from a timer or a service, but it hides plain fields changed outside the template.

nodes.title: Keep the count in one signal
nodes.why: The count is the only state; reading count() in the template ties the number and the minus button to it.
nodes.alternative: A plain count = 0 field that the click handlers change.
nodes.tradeoff: A plain field works while every change starts with a click in this template; the signal also covers timers, services or a parent under OnPush or zoneless change detection.

nodes.title: Derive the disabled state
nodes.why: The minus button binds its disabled state to isZero(), which recalculates only when count changes.
nodes.alternative: Repeat count() === 0 in the template, or use a getter.
nodes.tradeoff: An inline expression is shorter, but a named computed keeps the zero rule in one place for the template and anything else that needs it.

nodes.title: Clamp the decrement at zero
nodes.why: The disabled button stops clicks at 0, and the clamp keeps the count from going negative for any other caller of dec().
nodes.alternative: Rely on the disabled button alone, or return early when isZero() is true.
nodes.tradeoff: The clamp is one expression that cannot go below zero; an early return reads closer to the rule but repeats the zero check.

nodes.title: Reset with set
nodes.why: reset() replaces the value outright, so set says it directly; update derives the next value from the current one.
nodes.tradeoff: Both give the same value; set states the intent and skips reading the old count.
